test_cases.title: Verify that toggling a published pillar card to Inactive removes it from the Home Page without deleting the record
test_cases.description: A live, published Vision card is toggled to Inactive rather than deleted.

Save, publish, and refresh cache.
Load the Home Page carousel, then reopen the CMS pillar card list.
steps.expected: Vision no longer appears on the Home Page, but the Vision card record still exists in the CMS pillar card list (not deleted).

steps.expected: The Strategic Direction section does not render anywhere on the Home Page.

test_cases.title: Verify that an Active pillar card does not render when its parent Section is Unpublished
test_cases.description: Pillar Card status and Section status are independent objects.

Set the parent section to Unpublished.
Refresh cache and load the Home Page.
steps.expected: Neither the section nor the Vision card renders on the Home Page.

test_cases.title: Verify that a published edit is not visible to visitors until the cache is refreshed
test_cases.description: Relation edge case between content state and cache state.

steps.action: Edit and publish a change to the Mission pillar title.
Immediately load the Home Page before any cache refresh trigger.
steps.expected: The Home Page still shows the pre-edit title (stale cache).

steps.action: After the cache refresh interval/trigger, reload the Home Page.
steps.expected: After cache refresh, the Home Page shows the updated title.

test_cases.title: Verify that concurrent edits by two Site Content Editors on the same pillar card do not corrupt data
test_cases.description: Two editors open the same Vision card simultaneously and save different changes.

steps.action: Editor A opens the Vision pillar card and changes the title.
steps.expected: Editor A's form shows the original data.

steps.action: Editor B opens the same Vision pillar card (before Editor A saves) and changes the description.
steps.expected: Editor B's form also shows the original data (pre-Editor-A-save).

steps.action: Editor A saves, then Editor B saves.
steps.expected: The final saved record is a well-formed, non-corrupted card (either last-write-wins cleanly or a conflict warning is shown) - no partially-merged or broken field values.

test_cases.title: Verify that deleting the currently-displayed pillar card does not break the frontend carousel
test_cases.description: The Mission card is deleted while it happens to be the card most recently viewed by cached visitors.

steps.action: Confirm the Mission card is Active and published.
Delete the Mission pillar card from the CMS.
Refresh cache and load the Home Page carousel, cycling through all cards.
steps.expected: The carousel shows only Vision and Objectives with no blank/broken slot where Mission used to be.

test_cases.title: Verify that toggling a card to Inactive mid-session does not leave a broken slot for a visitor mid-carousel-navigation
test_cases.description: Visitor is viewing the Mission card when an editor deactivates it in another session.

steps.action: Visitor loads the Home Page and navigates carousel to the Mission card.
In a separate CMS session, an editor sets Mission's Active Status to False and publishes.
steps.expected: Editor's change is published (cache not yet refreshed for the visitor's session).

steps.action: Visitor clicks the right arrow to move on from Mission.
steps.expected: Navigation proceeds without a JS error or blank card; on the visitor's next full page load (post cache-refresh), Mission no longer appears.

test_cases.title: Verify that carousel arrow navigation direction is mirrored correctly for Arabic (RTL)
test_cases.description: Confirms whether "right arrow = next" holds visually/functionally once the layout mirrors.

steps.action: Switch site language to Arabic.
Load the carousel on the Vision card.
steps.expected: Vision card displayed with arrow positions mirrored.

steps.action: Click the arrow in the visually-forward (mirrored) direction.
steps.expected: The visually-forward arrow (now on the left, per RTL mirroring) advances to the Mission card - navigation direction matches reading direction, not raw left/right DOM position.
